source_refs.note: Posterior Pituitary: a main subheading of 16.2.2 Pituitary Gland, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 61-62.

blocks.text: The posterior pituitary contains axons that originate in hypothalamus and extend to posterior pituitary. It does not synthesize any hormone but only stores and releases the hormones made by hypothalamus. The following are the hormones released by posterior pituitary.

items: Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH or vasopressin) stimulates water retention by the kidneys.
Oxytocin stimulates the milk-ejection by stimulating the contraction of smooth muscles of mammary glands. It also stimulates uterine contractions in women during childbirth.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: During embryonic development, posterior pituitary is formed from an outgrowth of neural tissue. That’s why, hypothalamus of brain and posterior pituitary remain interconnected by a tract of axons.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: Oxytocin secretion continues after childbirth in breast-feeding mothers. That’s why, the uterus of a nursing mother returns to its normal size after pregnancy more quickly than the mothers who do not breast-feed.

blocks.alt: The hypothalamus with its stalk and the two pituitary lobes, with blood vessels to the anterior lobe and axons of the hypothalamus to the posterior lobe. Green arrows from the anterior pituitary: TSH to the thyroid, ACTH to the adrenal cortex, FSH and LH to the ovary and to the testis, GH to bones and skeletal muscles, prolactin to the mammary glands. Red arrows from the posterior pituitary: oxytocin to the mammary glands and the uterus, ADH to the kidney.
blocks.caption: Figure 16.3: Hormones of anterior & posterior pituitary and their target sites (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 16.3; every anterior-lobe arrow drawn from the anterior lobe).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 16.3 draws the GH and prolactin arrows from beneath the posterior lobe; both are hormones of the anterior pituitary, so the drawing above takes them from the anterior lobe.
